title: The Crest Jewel of Discrimination
dateDisplay: c. 8th century CE (attributed to Shankara; date unsettled)
author: shankara
attributionNote: Attributed to Śaṅkara, the commentator of the Upanishads and founder of the Advaita school; modern scholarship doubts the attribution, since the poem's metre and teaching look later than his commentaries, but the tradition of the Advaita order has transmitted it under his name and reads it as his own instruction. GRETIL publishes the verses alone in the file's numbering.
description: The Vivekacūḍāmaṇi teaches the whole Advaita path in verse: the qualifications of the pupil and the marks of the teacher, the discrimination of the eternal from the transitory, the four means of liberation and the yearning for release, the five sheaths and the analysis of the self that is not body, breath or mind, the all-pervading consciousness witnessed in waking, dream and deep sleep, the identity of the self with Brahman, the removal of the ignorance the texts call beginningless, the renunciation that follows, and the joy of the one who knows. Its verses on the unbroken light of consciousness are the most quoted expression of Advaita in modern India.
historicalContext: Read in the Advaita monasteries as a manual for the disciple and translated by Śrī Chandrasekharendra Sarasvatī's line and by modern teachers such as Chinmayananda and Dayananda, the poem became the classical statement of Vedantic self-enquiry for a wider public than the commentaries commanded, and the library holds Śaṅkara's Upanishad commentaries from the same school as a second voice.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: 580 verses in the numbering the edition prints, streamed from GRETIL at read time and indexed in reading order. The file carries no reference abbreviation beside its verses and prints its own title above the opening invocation, which the library does not index as text. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
